newsitem.title: USA: Hundreds evacuated in Louisiana chlorine leak.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds evacuated in Louisiana chlorine leak.

text.p: More than 600 people, including 150 nursing home residents, were evacuated from a residential area in this small, north-central Louisiana town Wednesday night after a one-ton chlorine tank began leaking, authorities said.
No injuries were reported, police said.
The chlorine cylinder, used to treat well water for drinking, began leaking shortly before 6 p.m. and was still leaking at 11 p.m., State Police Master Trooper Howard McKee said.

"The leak is in a nipple between the tank and the shutoff valve, so it can't just be turned off. Hazardous materials units are trying to seal it with a sleeve so the tank can be off-loaded," McKee said. "We don't know if that will work."
The one-quarter mile evacuation area may have to be expanded if the wind picks up or shifts, he said. "Right now weather is our greatest potential enemy," McKee said.
The evacuees were taken to two shelters -- a high school gym and the parish courthouse.
